findings.chapter: Chapter 1 / It All Starts With the First Token
findings.evidence: "The vLLM FP8-KV blog post’s often-quoted ‘54%’ — from its Llama-3.1-8B Table 3 (vLLM blog, post dated 2026-04-22 — inside the 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff; retrieved 2026-11-15, an access date only, since access dates are not evidence dates, so no addendum revision applies) [S6] — is, on this book’s reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient [1P][HYPOTHESIS]."
findings.issue: The claim is labelled [1P][HYPOTHESIS], but the source is a vendor blog post, not a first-party model specification. The book's own provenance taxonomy defines [1P] as 'the model vendor's own spec' and [2°] as 'reputable second-hand.' A blog post interpreting a table is not a first-party specification for the 54% figure; it is an interpretation of a vendor claim. This is a provenance-label mismatch.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the label to [2°][HYPOTHESIS] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] and state explicitly that the 54% reading is the book's interpretation of a vendor blog, not a vendor-stated memory ratio.

findings.evidence: Page 32 (§1.1.5, KV cache as a concept): "At 9.2K input tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB on the input-only basis — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — and the 8-bit raw byte-halving variant is ~12.06 GB on that same input-only basis — 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB — against ~12.45 GB for the same 8-bit variant on the input-plus-output resident basis at 9.5K tokens, the basis Ch. 7 §3 uses for slot counting (9,500 × 1,310,720 B = 12,451,840,000 B ≈ 12.45 GB; the FP16 figure on that resident basis is ~24.9 GB, written 24.90368 GB there)."
findings.issue: The sentence compares the 8-bit per-request figure on the input-only basis (12.06 GB) against the 8-bit figure on the resident basis (12.45 GB) and the FP16 resident figure (~24.9 GB), but omits the FP16 input-only figure in the same comparison set, leaving the reader with a partially unpaired set of figures at exactly the point where the book is establishing its two named bases. More importantly, the cross-reference "Ch. 7 §3 uses for slot counting" resolves to a subsection that is titled §7.3 "Worked Example" (page 162–169, heading "7.3. Worked Example"), not to the subsection that actually derives the slot count. The slot-counting rule ("the canonical concurrency ceiling is that resident-basis quotient floored to a whole slot — 17, not 18") and the concurrency ceiling itself are stated in Ch. 4 §4.6 (page 120: "~17 full-context requests once the ~64 GB runtime is reserved: 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB ≈ 17.5, floored to 17"), in Ch. 7 §3 (page 168: "17.51; conservative integer floor 17") and in Ch. 7 Fig 7.7 ("The concurrency budget", listed in the List of Figures at page 9 as being on page 168). The book's own cross-reference convention (Preface, page 23) states that "§ N.M (the thin space after § is optional, so §7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference), which means Chapter N, Section M". So "Ch. 7 §3" is a legal form pointing at §7.3, but the citation is ambiguous about which figure it supports: the same paragraph also asserts "written 24.90368 GB there", which appears in Ch. 7 §3 (Table 7-1: "9,500 × 2,621,440 B = 24,903,680,000 B ≈ 24.90 GB"), so the reference does resolve. The residual defect is the missing FP16 input-only figure in the comparison set and the lack of a named slot-count rule at the point of citation — a reader arriving at the eight-bit figure cannot see the FP16/8-bit pairing on a single basis.
findings.fix_instruction: Complete the comparison set in the Ch. 1 §1.1.5 paragraph by stating the FP16 input-only figure alongside the 8-bit input-only figure on the same basis (i.e. ~24.12 GB FP16 vs ~12.06 GB at 8-bit, input-only; ~24.90 GB FP16 vs ~12.45 GB at 8-bit, resident), and name the slot-count rule explicitly at the point of citation (e.g. "the whole-slot floor of 17 that Ch. 7 §3 and Ch. 17 apply") so the reader is pointed at the rule, not only at the number's location.

findings.evidence: "...the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M ([1P][FACT] model cards: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; HF zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10)". The book's own convention (PDF p.24, Preface, Cross-references): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A"; the compliant form is used consistently elsewhere ("Appendix A §9A" on PDF pp.33, 44, 53, 77).
findings.issue: Malformed appendix section cross-reference: "Appendix A §10" carries no letter suffix and therefore contradicts the Preface's declared appendix-section convention (letter-suffixed labels such as §9A). It is the only bare-numbered appendix section reference in the visible text and cannot be resolved unambiguously by a reader following the stated convention.
findings.fix_instruction: Change "Appendix A §10" to the letter-suffixed form (e.g. "Appendix A §10A" or whatever the target section's actual letter-suffixed label is), and verify the target exists in Appendix A; sweep Appendix A-facing references for any other bare-numbered section refs.

findings.evidence: Figure 1.1: The KV cache: every token adds one K/V per layer per head — for a generated token, written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled; prompt-token K/V is written during prefill.
findings.issue: This is a complex description of when K/V is written for generated tokens. The text says 'written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled'. A token sampled at step t is processed as input at step t+1. This is correct but verbose and potentially confusing for an intro figure.
findings.fix_instruction: Simplify the figure caption to 'Generated token K/V is appended during the next step's forward pass.' This matches the visual of the loop in Fig 2.1.
